title: Location Data Exposure
description: Child's device (EE2) transmits live GPS coordinates to the backend (P1) at regular intervals. This exposes the user's precise location to the backend, which could be used for tracking, profiling, or unauthorized access.

title: Location Data Inference
description: The backend (P1) may infer the child's location from the GPS coordinates transmitted by the device (EE2). This inference could lead to the creation of a profile based on the child's location.

title: Location Data Non-Repudiation
description: The transmission of GPS coordinates by the device (EE2) to the backend (P1) may not be reproducible or verifiable by the child, as the device is an external entity.

title: Location Data Disclosure
description: The backend (P1) may disclose the child's location (EE2) to third parties or for internal use, as the data is transmitted over a network.

title: Location Data Disclosure (Device)
description: The device (EE2) may disclose the child's location to the backend (P1) without the child's knowledge or consent, as the device is an external entity.

title: Location Data Uncertainty
description: The accuracy of the GPS coordinates transmitted by the device (EE2) may be uncertain due to signal interference, GPS signal degradation, or other factors.

title: Location Data Non-Compliance
description: The transmission of GPS coordinates by the device (EE2) to the backend (P1) may violate privacy policies or regulations regarding location data.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location Data
description: The backend process (P1) writes location pings to the Location History Store (DS1). If the backend has access to the raw location data or the ability to modify the store, an attacker could potentially access or alter this data. This is a potential leak of sensitive location information.

title: Data Exfiltration
description: The backend process (P1) writes data to the Location History Store (DS1). If the backend has access to the raw location data or the ability to modify the store, an attacker could potentially exfiltrate this data.

title: Unauthorized Location Pings
description: Mobile App (P1) sends new location pings to the backend without explicit user consent or a clear, opt-in mechanism for the user to review and approve each ping.
assumptions: The app assumes the user has granted location permissions.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the app provides a visible 'Allow' or 'Deny' toggle for each ping, or if it relies on a blanket permission.

title: Data Exfiltration Risk
description: The backend (P2) receives and stores the raw location data from P1. If P2 is not configured with strict data retention policies or if the data is not encrypted in transit and at rest, this flow poses a significant risk of data leakage.
assumptions: The backend does not have a mechanism to delete location data after a specific period.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the backend has a data deletion policy or if the data is automatically purged.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2) processes the incoming location data. If the engine is not configured to only process data from authorized sources or if it logs the data unnecessarily, it could be used for unauthorized profiling or surveillance.
assumptions: The engine logs all incoming location data without any filtering or masking.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the engine has a mechanism to filter or mask location data before processing.

title: Unauthorized Access to Family Account
description: An attacker could potentially access the Family Account Store (DS2) and read the configured zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) without explicit authorization, potentially compromising the integrity of the data.
assumptions: The Family Account Store is not encrypted or has weak access controls.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard security practices are not in place.

title: Data Leakage to Unauthorized Parties
description: The Family Account Store (DS2) could be accessed by an unauthorized party, leading to the leakage of sensitive user data (e.g., home address, school location, friend's house) to malicious actors.
assumptions: The data is not protected by strong encryption or access controls.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard security practices are not in place.

title: Unauthorized Access to Geofencing Engine
description: An attacker could potentially access the Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2) and read the configured zone definitions, potentially compromising the integrity of the data.
assumptions: The Geofencing Engine is not encrypted or has weak access controls.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard security practices are not in place.

title: Data Leakage to Unauthorized Parties

assumptions: The data is not protected by strong encryption or access controls.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard security practices are not in place.

title: Unauthorized Geofencing Access
description: The process P2 (Geofencing & Alert Engine) has the capability to push notifications to the parent entity EE1 without explicit authorization or user consent. This allows P2 to potentially access or manipulate EE1's location data or trigger alerts based on arbitrary conditions.

title: Data Leakage via Notification
description: The process P2 may inadvertently leak sensitive location data or personal information to the parent entity EE1 through the notification mechanism, especially if the notification payload includes detailed location coordinates or personal identifiers.

title: Parent Entity Unauthorized Access
description: The parent entity EE1 may have unauthorized access to the process P2 or its data flows, allowing it to trigger or manipulate the geofencing logic without proper oversight.
